components.css: .ds-release { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 11rem minmax(0, 1fr); column-gap: 2rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); } .ds-year { position: sticky; top: 5rem; margin: 0; font-size: 1.875rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: var(--color-accent); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-rel-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.875rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.15; letter-spacing: -0.025em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-rel-meta { margin: 0.5rem 0 0; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--color-ink-subtle); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-rel-meta span + span::before { content: '·'; margin: 0 0.5rem; } .ds-rel-note { margin: 1.5rem 0 0; font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.45; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--color-ink); max-width: 44ch; } .ds-rel-desc { margin: 1rem 0 0; line-height: 1.65; color: var(--color-ink-muted); max-width: 64ch; } .ds-rel-shot { margin-top: 2rem; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; border: 1px solid var(--color-rule); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--color-paper-2); } .ds-rel-label { margin: 2rem 0 0; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-rel-list { list-style: none; margin: 0.75rem 0 0; padding: 0; } .ds-rel-list li { position: relative; padding: 0.25rem 0 0.25rem 1.25rem; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--color-ink-muted); } .ds-rel-list li::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0.95em; width: 0.5rem; height: 1px; background: var(--color-ink-subtle); } .ds-rel-visit { display: inline-block; margin-top: 1.5rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-ink); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--color-rule-strong); text-underline-offset: 0.22em; } .ds-rel-visit:hover { color: var(--color-accent); text-decoration-color: currentColor; }

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a well-kept product changelog from a careful tech company. Every system he built is a dated release: a title, a meta line, a short first-person note, what it does, a screenshot, what shipped, what it was built with, and a link out. The page is white, the ink is near-black, the secondary text is cool slate, and the only structure is a 1px hairline. One warm orange marks what to do and when things happened; nothing else is colored.

Density is moderate and editorial: generous vertical air between releases, tight measure inside them (44 to 64ch). The hero is type only, with no image, no works list and no card. Below it, every section shares one grammar: a left rail 11rem wide holding a date or a label, and the content column to its right. In the works changelog the year in that rail stays pinned while its releases scroll past; that positional stick is the signature interaction, and nothing else on the page moves except colour on hover.

The voice is first person throughout, and the visual system stays out of its way: no decorative devices, no costume type, no ornament between the reader and the work.
keyCharacteristics: White page (near-black in dark mode), near-black ink, slate secondary, hairline rules only.
One warm orange, reserved for the primary action, date and year markers, link hover and the mobile header contact.
One grotesk (Schibsted Grotesk, 400 to 800) with tabular figures for dates; no mono.
An 11rem rail on the left, content on the right, in every section.
Sticky year marker in the works changelog; no other motion beyond hover colour.
8px radius on buttons and screenshots, 6px on small controls; no shadows, gradients or glass.

rules.name: The Orange Means Act-or-When Rule
rules.body: Orange appears only on the primary action, on date and year markers, on link hover, and on the mobile header contact. A non-date rail label is Pale Slate, never orange. If an orange element is neither something to click nor a point in time, it is wrong.

rules.name: The One Primary Per Viewport Rule
rules.body: On desktop the header contact is a quiet underlined link so the hero's orange button is the only filled primary in the first viewport. On mobile, where the nav is gone, the header contact becomes the compact orange button.

rules.name: The Tabular Dates Rule
rules.body: Every year, period and date run in tabular figures so changelog dates align like a ledger.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a heading. Section titles, release titles and the hero name open their blocks directly; context goes beneath in a note or meta row.

rules.name: The Hairline Only Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with a 1px rule and nothing else. If a surface needs separating, draw a hairline; never a grey band, a shadow or a blur.

dos: Do put every section below the hero on the 11rem rail plus content column, with the section title starting at the page edge.
Do keep orange to the primary action, date and year markers, link hover and the mobile header contact.
Do separate everything with 1px hairlines on plain Paper.
Do set dates, years and periods in tabular figures.
Do write each release with a first-person note under its meta row.
Do limit motion to colour change on hover (120ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)).
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above any heading.
Don't colour a non-date rail label orange; use Pale Slate.
Don't add a second filled primary to the desktop first viewport; the header contact stays a quiet link there.
Don't use grey section bands, shadows, gradients or glass.
Don't slide, fade or animate anything into view; the sticky year is positional only.
Don't introduce a second typeface or a monospace costume for dates or code.
